full_text:
A peasant woman named Catherine was so exceedingly lazy that whenever she was supposed to spin flax into thread, she spun it so poorly that the reel was full of knots. When her husband scolded her for not winding the yarn onto a reel, Catherine had a ready excuse: "How can I wind yarn when we have no wooden reel? Go into the forest and chop timber to make me one!"

The husband went into the forest to chop hazel wood for a reel. Catherine secretly ran ahead, hid in a thicket, and sang in an eerie voice: "He who cuts wood for a reel shall choke to death; he who winds yarn shall never draw breath!"

Terrified that the forest spirits were warning him of mortal danger, the husband dropped his axe and ran home, swearing never to speak of a reel again.

Next, Catherine placed the tangled boiled yarn into a pot with an old dead sparrow. When the husband asked for his dinner, he pulled out the bird. "See!" cried Catherine. "Even the pot knows that yarn should not be wound; the thread has turned into a feathered bird!"

The gullible husband marveled at the wonder, swore off linen altogether, and Catherine sat merrily by the fire, laughing at how easily a sharp tongue and a little cunning can turn lazy hours into peaceful rest.
moral: A clever rogue can invent endless excuses to avoid work, but true prosperity comes from honest effort.
